pr_body:
Closes #4345 

Similar to seat command, this provides an alias for the current output.
Instead of the output name or identifier, `-` can be used to operate on
the focused output by name and `--` can be used to operate on the
focused output by its identifier. This will prevent operating on the
no-op output when using either alias.

issue_context.title: Feature request: Transform current output
issue_context.body:
## What

Ability to transform the current screen without specifying the name explicitly. Perhaps by allowing the `<name>` to be ommited. 

## Why

This would make it easier to bindsym to simple changes like `transform 90 clockwise`.

## Background

I currently have the following in my config to handle screen rotation and moving workpaces between outputs:

```bash
    # Move workspace to other screens
    bindsym $mod+Shift+w exec $term_run "source ~/.fzf.zsh && swaymsg -t get_outputs | jq -r '.[] | select(.focused!=true) | [.name, .make, .model] | @tsv' | fzf --select-1 --reverse --prompt='Move workspace to:' | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -r swaymsg move workspace to"
    bindsym $mod+Alt+w exec swaymsg -t get_outputs | jq '.[] | select(.focused!=true) | .name' | head -n1 | xargs swaymsg move workspace to

    # Rotate current workspace
    bindsym $mod+Shift+r exec swaymsg -t get_outputs | jq '.[] | select(.focused==true) | .name' | xargs -I% swaymsg output % transform 90 clockwise
```

review_comments: The right side of the `||` will always be true when the left side is true and can be omitted
strcmp will take the null terminator into account, so it won't. That would be true with strncmp.
